items.title: Client, server aur API: kaun maangta hai, kaun deta hai
items.one_idea: A client (your phone or browser) sends a request, a server (a computer that serves) sends back a response, and an API is the agreed set of rules that says how to ask and what comes back.
items.spoken_hook: Instagram खोलते ही feed कहाँ से आती है?
items.hook_formula: direct_question: an everyday app moment as one short question, answered in the next line
items.visual_idea: Phone left, rack right, REQUEST arrow, RESPONSE card; restaurant strip; Mars crossed out of the menu; server box turning into CLIENT box.
items.everyday_anchor: A restaurant: you (client) order from the menu, the waiter (API) carries the order by the menu's rules, the kitchen (server) cooks and sends the dish back.
items.example: EXAMPLE: weather app: phone asks 'weather for Pune', server answers 28 degree.
facts_to_verify: Client starts the request, server answers (MDN HTTP Overview).
A server is not necessarily one machine.
API = set of features and rules, a contract (MDN Glossary API).
No company-specific claim; no HTTP verbs or status codes.
keywords: what is an api in hindi
request response kaise kaam karta hai

items.title: Website kholte hi andar kya hota hai
items.one_idea: When you type a web address and press enter, the browser looks up the server's address (DNS), connects, asks for the page (HTTP request), gets the HTML back, then asks for the images, styles and scripts it names, and draws the page.
items.spoken_hook: वेबसाइट slow हो, तो तुम तुरंत छोड़ देते हो।
items.hook_formula: relatable_stake: a slow site you abandon
items.cover_headline: What Happens When You Open a Website
items.visual_idea: A browser bar on the left and a server rack on the right; a path of stops lights up in order; a clock strip fills as each stop adds time.
items.everyday_anchor: Ordering a courier parcel: find the shop's address (DNS), call and connect, place the order (request), get the box (HTML), extra items arrive in separate deliveries.
items.example: EXAMPLE: a shopping site: the first reply is the HTML, then dozens of image and script requests follow.
facts_to_verify: Order: DNS lookup, connection, HTTP GET, HTML back, more requests for sub-resources, render (MDN How browsers work).
No eight-round-trips claim, no abandon-time number, no company claim, no other-day reference.
keywords: website kholne par kya hota hai
what happens when you type a url in browser

items.title: DNS: naam se machine ka address kaise milta hai
items.one_idea: DNS (Domain Name System) turns a name like example.com into the IP address of a machine: your device checks its own memory (cache) first, then asks a resolver, which asks the root, then the .com (TLD) servers, then the domain's own (authoritative) server, and every answer is cached for a limited time (TTL).
items.spoken_hook: Phone को google.com का address पता ही नहीं होता।
items.hook_formula: surprising_fact: the viewer's own phone does not know the address of the site it opens
items.hook_source: hook-writer surprising_fact; sourced on MDN What is a domain name
items.visual_idea: A phone with a name label on the left, a server rack on the right with an IP number on it; between them resolver, root, TLD, authoritative boxes light up one by one, each handing the next a pointer, and the final IP number flies back to the phone; a small clock chip on the cache copy counts down.
items.everyday_anchor: Phone contacts: you tap a name, not a number.
items.example: EXAMPLE: example.com resolves to 93.184.216.34 (label as EXAMPLE).
items.cover_headline: How a Name Finds a Machine
facts_to_verify: DNS is a hierarchical and decentralized naming system that translates a domain name to an IP address (MDN Glossary DNS) - verified.
Browser first asks the local DNS cache; if unknown, asks a DNS server (MDN) - verified.
Resolver asks root, .com TLD answers with the domain's name servers, authoritative returns the IP, resolver caches it (AWS Route 53) - verified.
TTL is a time limit on caching (RFC 1034 3.6) - verified. No TTL numbers.
Changes reach caches only after old copies expire; say 'some time'.
